mainEntity.name: Do you provide assisted living & senior living cleaning in Peabody, MA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Peabody (Essex County) is one of the 109 Massachusetts cities and towns we serve. It is about 32 miles northeast of our Marlborough base in a straight line. Every engagement starts with a free on-site assessment; call (978) 307-8107.

mainEntity.name: Which Peabody ZIP codes do you cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: All of them: 01960, 01961. If your facility sits on a town line, tell us the street address and we will confirm.

mainEntity.name: Are there assisted living residences in Peabody?

acceptedAnswer.text: We have not verified one inside Peabody. The typical healthcare setting here is community hospital with a 24/7 ED plus a large suburban medical office cluster. If you operate a assisted living residence in town, we can schedule it on the same route as neighbouring towns.

mainEntity.name: What is explicitly outside your scope in a resident's unit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Anything that touches the resident or their possessions in a care capacity. We do not provide personal care, assist with transfers, handle personal laundry unless it is a separately contracted linen service, sort or discard belongings, clean inside refrigerators or cupboards without written permission, handle medications or medication carts, or move furniture that a resident relies on for orientation. Clutter that blocks our cleaning gets reported, not resolved by us. Drawing this boundary in the contract protects the residence too: it keeps a cleaning contractor from performing tasks 651 CMR reserves for trained residence staff.

mainEntity.name: Are you insured at a level that satisfies our risk manager?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dory's Cleaning Services Inc. carries $2 million general liability, and we issue a certificate naming the residence as additional insured before the first shift. Workers' compensation covers our employees — we staff with employees rather than subcontractors, which keeps liability and training accountability in one place. What we do not claim is a license or certification to clean healthcare facilities, because Massachusetts does not issue one; any vendor telling you otherwise is describing something that does not exist. What is verifiable is insurance, employee training records, and documented protocols, and those are what we put in front of your risk manager.

mainEntity.name: Blood and body-fluid spills happen in the units. Who cleans those, and under what standard?

acceptedAnswer.text: 29 CFR 1910.1030 governs it, and it carries weight in this sector: federal OSHA issued 9 citations across 3 assisted living inspections between October 2024 and September 2025, with $37,006 in penalties — the largest penalty total of any standard for assisted living. Our staff are trained and equipped for environmental decontamination of spills: PPE, absorb, clean, then disinfect with an EPA-registered product at label contact time, with contaminated waste bagged per your regulated-waste policy. If the incident involves a resident who is still being attended, care staff manage the resident first and call us to the surface afterward.

Citations Peabody assisted living residences can avoid

Real, published regulatory findings — every citation links to its source.

29 CFR 1910.1030 — OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens

Bloodborne pathogens programme deficiencies — exposure control plan, contaminated laundry, regulated waste, surface decontamination and PPE.

Federal OSHA, October 2024 to September 2025: 9 citations across 3 inspections of assisted living facilities, carrying $37,006 in penalties — the largest penalty total of any standard for the sector.

651 CMR 12.04(12)

No adequate plan to prevent and limit the spread of communicable disease. Every Massachusetts residence must have one, conforming to accepted principles of universal precautions based on DPH guidance.

651 CMR 12.09 — Compliance Reviews of Assisted Living Residences

Common-area housekeeping is inspected directly by the state. Massachusetts compliance reviews happen at least every two years and must include a physical inspection of the residence's common areas.

Our sequence, step by step

  1. Coordinate memory-care cleaning with staff so routines and residents are not disrupted.
  2. Escalate cleaning during respiratory or gastrointestinal illness as directed by the residence.
  3. Keep laundry and food-service areas to their own cleaning procedures.
  4. Damp-mop floors with wet-floor signage to reduce fall risk.
  5. Log apartments and common areas completed.

How often

  • Illness outbreaks: escalated as the residence directs.
  • Periodic: carpets, windows and high dusting.

Assisted living residences are cleaned during the day, scheduled around meals, activities and residents' preferences.
